title: A page for newcomers, read by four invented visitors before Dinis saw it
span: 11 November, 09:50 to 10:15 UTC; open until Dinis says yes
summary: At about 09:50 Dinis looked at the site and said the first page must be "super clear", for a journalist or anyone who does not know what this is; and asked to simulate four visitors. Three and a half minutes later a new agent, synthetic@, had written four invented people; it read the old front page first, so the draft would have something to be better than. The envoy drafted /welcome/ at 09:57, the designer framed it, the invented visitors read the draft, the envoy rewrote it from their findings, and a third run found the summit's decision in about 9 seconds. Twenty minutes, three readings, no person in the loop: the page waits at /welcome/ for Dinis's yes.

welcome/ rewritten from the readers: the latest decision on the first screen, what a person checks and what goes live without one, the 22 minutes said plainly (run 2's findings 1, 4, 5)

a trace of the loop ("a front page for newcomers, drafted, read by four invented visitors and rewritten in 14 minutes")

the journal's twelfth piece, "Read before he saw it", from that trace

pauses_note: No pause of three minutes or more after the agents started: the loop turned every two to four minutes. Its one open step is Dinis's: the page moves to / only on his yes, and that is not in the record.
shows: A loop with invented readers: draft, read by four personas, rewrite from their ranked findings, read again: three readings in twelve minutes, before the one real reader it was for.
The personas were written before the first run, and the old page was read first: the test was set before the thing it tested.
Words, frame and reading are three agents with three folders (welcome/, the frame, research/synthetic/); none edits another's, and each step is a commit.
reading: The reporter's trace of the loop (10:09:41) and run 3 (10:09:58) were written in parallel: the trace closes on run 2's rewrite, and run 3 came 17 s after it.
Invented visitors are a tool, said so on every page they appear on; nothing here says what real readers think.
